item.text: {"search_note":"I did not find reliable 2024 evidence that Srettha voluntarily opened campaign-finance records, invited independent audits of campaign spending, or proactively released concealed government decisions. The best available evidence is indirect: asset disclosure, some live press scrutiny, and formal court review, offset by journalist arrests and the ethics case around Pichit Chuenban.","evidence":[{"title":"Bangkok Post asset-declaration report","publisher":"Bangkok Post","date":"June 17, 2024","url":"https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/politics/2812379/declaration","summary":"Srettha and his wife publicly declared substantial assets to the anti-corruption commission. This is weak positive evidence that he tolerated some external scrutiny of personal finances.","question_ids":["7B.6"]},{"title":"Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2024, Thailand","publisher":"Reuters Institute for the Study of Journalism","date":"June 17, 2024","url":"https://reutersinstitute.politics.ox.ac.uk/digital-news-report/2024/thailand","summary":"The report says Thai media could still criticize government policy and report corruption, and that mainstream outlets continued verification work. This is the best positive evidence that independent scrutiny of the government still existed under Srettha.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.2"]},{"title":"Thai journalists arrested over news coverage","publisher":"Reuters via Yahoo News","date":"February 13, 2024","url":"https://www.yahoo.com/news/thai-journalists-arrested-news-coverage-054141721.html","summary":"Two journalists were arrested over reporting on anti-royal graffiti, and Reuters quoted Srettha saying the government was fair on press freedom and that there was no harassment. The contemporaneous arrests make this strong negative evidence for tolerance of independent investigation.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.2"]},{"title":"Thailand: New government slow to protect rights","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"January 11, 2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/01/11/thailand-new-government-slow-protect-rights","summary":"HRW said the new government had not made serious rights reforms and should end politically motivated prosecutions of peaceful protesters and monarchy critics. This is negative evidence on tolerance of independent scrutiny of associates and conflicts of interest.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.5"]},{"title":"Thai court says PM Srettha violated rules on ethics in cabinet appointment","publisher":"Reuters via ThePrint","date":"August 14, 2024","url":"https://theprint.in/world/thai-court-says-pm-srettha-violated-rules-on-ethics-in-cabinet-appointment/2222960/","summary":"Reuters reported that the Constitutional Court said Srettha violated ethical rules in appointing a cabinet minister who had served prison time. This is the strongest negative item for tolerance of independent investigation into associates and conflicts of interest.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.5"]},{"title":"Srettha removed by Constitutional Court","publisher":"Thailand Public Relations Department","date":"August 14, 2024","url":"https://thailand.prd.go.th/en/content/category/detail/id/48/iid/315614","summary":"The state said Srettha was removed by the Constitutional Court for violating ethical standards after the Pichit appointment. This does not prove voluntary tolerance, but it does show he was subject to and did not evade institutional review.","question_ids":["7B.6","7B.5"]}]}
